rationale: The candidate reads as a compact, mostly box-derived mass with a scalloped top, but the form remains weak in plan/section and does not yet establish a convincing active ground threshold. Across the four views it is somewhat coherent as one object, yet the silhouette feels arbitrary rather than programmatic: there is no meaningful carved void, court, or undercut responding to the verified access edge, and the mass does not visibly organize neighborhood-living publicness at the ground. The stepped/irregular upper outline is not enough to carry the brief; it reads more like a decorative profile than a capacity-bearing section. Reference set points toward public courtyards, perimeter cuts, or bridge-linked openings, but the candidate currently lacks those spatial relations. Overall it is not program-fit because neighborhood_living requires an active public edge, at least one legible void/terrace, and upper massing that varies without erasing the ground relation.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise massing with a central void and a legible bridge/connector can support a public neighborhood program.
